title: Corporate mission, vision and strategic business units
summary: The mission states why a firm exists, the vision where it wants to go. A strategic business unit is a business that can stand on its own, with its own competitors and a manager.

chunks.heading: Corporate mission versus vision
chunks.explanation_md:
Step 1 of corporate planning is **defining the corporate mission**.

A **mission** is a clear, concise and enduring statement of the reasons for an organization's existence. It is often called the **core purpose** and gives employees and management a shared sense of purpose, direction and opportunity.

**Vision versus mission:**

- A **vision** statement outlines what the organization aspires to become or achieve in the long-term future. It is the ultimate goal or dream.
- A **mission** statement defines the organization's purpose and primary objectives.

The professor's example is the business school itself. Its vision: to be a premier business school of impactful ideas for influencing management education and business practices relevant to the emerging needs of industry, economy and society. Its mission: to develop globally sensitive, excellence seeking management professionals with a social entrepreneurial mindset.

key_terms.meaning: A clear, concise and enduring statement of the reasons for an organization's existence; its core purpose.
What an organization aspires to become or achieve in the long-term future.

chunks.exam_line: Mission = purpose and primary objectives (why we exist). Vision = long-term aspiration (what we want to become).

chunks.heading: Mission statements of real companies
chunks.explanation_md:
The slides show three company pages that state a purpose or mission:

- A food-delivery company page with the line **Better food for more people**.
- Nike: **to bring inspiration and innovation to every athlete in the world** (with a note that if you have a body, you are an athlete).
- The Coca-Cola Company: purpose **Refresh the world. Make a difference.** Its vision is to craft the brands and choice of drinks that people love, to refresh them in body and spirit, in ways that create a more sustainable business and a better shared future.

Notice the Coca-Cola page lists a **purpose** and a **vision** separately, which matches the vision versus mission split.
chunks.exam_line: Examples of mission or purpose: Nike (inspiration and innovation to every athlete); Coca-Cola (Refresh the world. Make a difference.).

chunks.heading: Strategic business units (SBUs)
chunks.explanation_md:
Step 2 is **establishing strategic business units** (SBU's). A **strategic business unit (SBU)**:

- is a single business, or a collection of related businesses, that **can exist separately** from the rest of the company
- has its **own set of competitors**
- has a **manager** responsible for strategic planning and profit performance

Examples from the slides:

- **P&G** has five sector business units: Baby, Feminine and Family Care; Beauty; Health Care; Grooming; Fabric and Home Care.
- **TATA** is shown with a list of businesses: Airlines, Motors, FMCG, Communications, Finance, Insurance, Real estate, Tata Power, Hospitality, Consultancy and Retail.

key_terms.meaning: A single business or collection of related businesses that can exist separately, has its own competitors and a manager responsible for strategic planning and profit.

chunks.exam_line: SBU: can exist separately, own competitors, own manager responsible for planning and profit. Examples: P&G's five sector units, TATA's many businesses.

questions.stem: Differentiate between a vision and a mission statement.
questions.model_answer_md:
| Basis | Vision | Mission |
|---|---|---|
| Meaning | What the organization aspires to become or achieve in the long-term future | Purpose and primary objectives; reasons for existence |
| Nature | The ultimate goal or dream | Clear, concise, enduring statement; core purpose |
| Role | Aspiration | Gives employees and management a shared sense of purpose, direction and opportunity |

Example: the business school's vision is to be a premier business school of impactful ideas, and its mission is to develop globally sensitive, excellence seeking management professionals.

questions.stem: Explain the corporate mission and the role of strategic business units in corporate planning.
questions.model_answer_md:
Strategic planning happens at corporate, division, business and product levels. At the corporate and division level the activities are defining the mission, establishing strategic business units, assigning resources and assessing growth opportunities.

**Corporate mission.** A clear, concise and enduring statement of the reasons for an organization's existence, also called its core purpose. It gives employees and management a shared sense of purpose, direction and opportunity. It differs from the **vision**, which is the long-term aspiration. Examples: Nike's mission to bring inspiration and innovation to every athlete in the world; the Coca-Cola purpose Refresh the world. Make a difference.

**Strategic business units.** An SBU is a single business or collection of related businesses that can exist separately, has its own competitors and has a manager responsible for planning and profit. P&G's five sector business units and TATA's many businesses are the slide examples. The firm then assesses each SBU's competitive advantage and market attractiveness to allocate resources.

**Conclusion.** The mission says why the firm exists, and SBUs divide the firm into businesses that can be planned separately.
